content: CIZ1, also known as Cip1-interacting zinc finger protein, is a protein in humans encoded by the CIZ1 gene. The protein encoded by the CIZ1 gene functions as a zinc finger DNA-binding transcription factor. It interacts specifically with CIP1 (also referred to as p21/CDKN1A), which is a component of a complex involving cyclin E. This protein may play a role in regulating the cellular localization of CIP1. In terms of clinical significance, an altered circulating form of the CIZ1 protein is produced by lung cancer cells, even at very early stages of the disease. Therefore, the detection of this specific protein variant in the blood has potential utility as a biomarker for the early detection of lung cancer. CIZ1 has been demonstrated to interact with the protein p21.
